description: Steps 7 and 8 of docs/the-delivery-loop.md: a reviewed branch validated on the real candidate, merged on the forge, and reconciled with its pull request. The mandate is one JSON object naming the repo and the branch, with base and forge_repo optional; an unsaid base is the trunk the repository declares. The latest review recorded by review-a-pinned-commit must be clean, and the flow refuses when the branch head, local or remote, differs from the reviewed commit. The combined tree is built on the current remote trunk in a locked worktree of its own, and scripts/run-gates.sh runs letter A plus every applicable letter of docs/gates.md there with --no-fail-fast; a red line stops the run, and lines that need a person are handed to one. A person's green is recorded against the reviewed commit, so a run started again after the trunk moved counts those lines as covered and asks only for lines not yet approved. The policy is read from the trusted trunk; `ask` on merge or push hands the step to a person. Just before the merge the trunk is re-read, and a trunk that moved stops the run rather than validating something else; the publication gate runs on the candidate. The private-names check is posted from here, because only this machine holds the list. Once every check before the merge has passed, the status sailor/integrated is posted on the reviewed commit naming this run, and the merge step refuses without it. Nothing is pushed to the trunk: the flow waits for every check the forge requires, asks the forge to merge the pull request, and is complete only when the remote trunk carries the reviewed commit, the tree that landed is the one the gates ran on, and the host reports the pull request MERGED. Every forge call runs as the account in sailor.forgeAs.

with.command:
set -eu
git -C "$REPO" fetch -q --no-tags "$REMOTE_NAME"
trunk=$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify "refs/remotes/$REMOTE_NAME/$BASE^{commit}")
short=$(printf '%s' "$COMMIT" | cut -c1-12)
tree="$(dirname "$REPO")/$(basename "$REPO")-worktrees/integrate-$short"
if git -C "$REPO" merge-base --is-ancestor "$COMMIT" "$trunk"; then
    printf '{"tree":"","trunk":"%s","candidate":"%s","already":true}' "$trunk" "$trunk"
    exit 0
fi
if [ -e "$tree" ]; then
    git -C "$REPO" worktree unlock "$tree" 2>/dev/null || true
    git -C "$REPO" worktree remove --force "$tree" >&2
fi
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$tree")"
git -C "$REPO" worktree add --detach --lock --reason "integration of $COMMIT" "$tree" "$trunk" >&2
git -C "$tree" merge --no-ff --no-edit -m "Merge branch '$BRANCH'" "$COMMIT" >&2 || { git -C "$tree" merge --abort 2>/dev/null || true; echo "$BRANCH does not merge cleanly onto $BASE at $trunk" >&2; exit 1; }
candidate=$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse HEAD)
printf '{"tree":"%s","trunk":"%s","candidate":"%s","already":false}' "$tree" "$trunk" "$candidate"

set -eu
if [ "$ALREADY" = true ]; then
    printf '{"letters":"","ran":0,"red":0,"manual":0,"covered":0,"manual_pending":false,"green":true,"pending":[],"pending_digest":""}'
    exit 0
fi
# The resolver and its manifest are the trunk's: a change may not choose the gates that judge it.
script=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sailor-gates.XXXXXX")
manifest=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sailor-manifest.XXXXXX")
covered=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sailor-covered.XXXXXX")
approved=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sailor-approved.XXXXXX")
pending=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sailor-pending.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$script" "$manifest" "$covered" "$approved" "$pending"' EXIT
printf '%s' "$CHECKED" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("\n".join(str(item) for item in json.load(sys.stdin)))' > "$covered"
# A person's green holds for the reviewed change it was given for, however far the trunk has moved since.
printf '%s' "$APPROVED" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("\n".join(str(line) for record in json.load(sys.stdin) for line in record["value"]["lines"]))' > "$approved"
git -C "$REPO" show "$TRUNK_COMMIT:scripts/run-gates.sh" > "$script" || { echo "the trunk $TRUNK_COMMIT carries no scripts/run-gates.sh" >&2; exit 2; }
git -C "$REPO" show "$TRUNK_COMMIT:docs/gates.md" > "$manifest" || { echo "the trunk $TRUNK_COMMIT carries no docs/gates.md" >&2; exit 2; }
cd "$TREE"
code=0
summary=$(sh "$script" --no-fail-fast --base "$TRUNK_COMMIT" --manifest "$manifest" --covered "$covered" --approved "$approved" --pending "$pending") || code=$?
[ "$code" -ne 2 ] || exit 2
printf '%s' "$summary" | python3 -c '
import hashlib, json, sys
summary = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
lines = [line for line in open(sys.argv[1]).read().splitlines() if line]
summary["pending"] = lines
summary["pending_digest"] = hashlib.sha256("\n".join(lines).encode()).hexdigest()[:16] if lines else ""
print(json.dumps(summary))
' "$pending"
exit "$code"

$join: The gates of docs/gates.md that apply to the combined tree

include lines a person must run or confirm (the step log of «gates» names them). Run them there and approve with an output file holding {"green": true} only when every one passed; reject with what was red.

options.label: green
options.facts: every manual line ran in the combined tree and passed

options.label: red
options.facts: a manual line failed; nothing is pushed

with.command:
set -eu
printf '%s' "$SAID" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
said = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
if not isinstance(said, dict) or said.get("green") is not True:
    sys.exit("the person did not write green: true for the manual gates; nothing is pushed")
print(json.dumps({"confirmed": True}))
'

$join: The delivery policy read from the trusted trunk (commit
) asks a person before this flow may push the validated combined commit to the trunk. Approve with an output file holding {"authorized": true}, or reject with the reason.

options.label: authorize
options.facts: every check before this step passed on the recorded commit

options.label: refuse
options.facts: nothing outward has happened yet; the run stops here

with.command:
set -eu
# The list of private names lives only on this machine, so the forge cannot post
# this check for itself. Until it is posted the request stays blocked and the
# host says nothing about why.
cd "$REPO"
git -C "$REPO" fetch -q --no-tags "$REMOTE_NAME"
"$REPO/scripts/attest-private-names.sh" "$COMMIT" >&2
printf '{"attested":"%s","posted":true,"at":"%s"}' "$COMMIT" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"

set -eu
# The trunk requires sailor/integrated, and only this step posts it: a merge
# made by hand has no run to name.
cd "$REPO"
"$REPO/scripts/attest-integration.sh" "$COMMIT" "${SAILOR_RUN:-}" >&2
printf '{"on":"%s","run":"%s"}' "$COMMIT" "$SAILOR_RUN"

set -eu
cd "$REPO"
# An inherited GH_REPO would point a call at another repository: it goes before the first gh call.
unset GH_REPO
forge_as=$(git -C "$REPO" config --get sailor.forgeAs) || { echo "sailor.forgeAs is not declared on this tree: refusing to act as the machine's active account" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -n "$forge_as" ] || { echo "sailor.forgeAs is empty on this tree: refusing to act as the machine's active account" >&2; exit 1; }
env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_REPO gh auth token --user "$forge_as" >/dev/null || { echo "no forge token for the declared account $forge_as" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -z "${FORGE_REPO:-}" ] || export GH_REPO="$FORGE_REPO"
# An empty --user or an empty GH_TOKEN makes gh answer as the machine's active account.
forge() {
    who=$(git -C "$REPO" config --get sailor.forgeAs) && [ -n "$who" ] || { echo "sailor.forgeAs vanished from this tree: refusing" >&2; exit 1; }
    token=$(env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_REPO gh auth token --user "$who") && [ -n "$token" ] || { echo "no forge token for $who: refusing" >&2; exit 1; }
    if [ -n "${FORGE_REPO:-}" ]; then
        env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN -u GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN GH_REPO="$FORGE_REPO" GH_TOKEN="$token" gh "$@"
    else
        env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN -u GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN -u GH_REPO GH_TOKEN="$token" gh "$@"
    fi
}
if [ "$ALREADY" = true ]; then
    printf '{"merged":"","asked":false}'
    exit 0
fi
[ "$POSTED_ON" = "$COMMIT" ] || { echo "no sailor/integrated on $COMMIT: nothing is merged" >&2; exit 1; }
# **THE TRUNK REFUSES A PUSH.** The forge merges once every required check is
# green, so this waits, one hour for every wait together.
tries=0
settle() {
    while :; do
        pending=$(forge pr checks "$NUMBER" --json bucket --jq '[.[] | select(.bucket == "pending")] | length') || { echo "cannot read the checks of pull request $NUMBER" >&2; exit 2; }
        [ "$pending" = 0 ] && break
        tries=$((tries + 1))
        [ "$tries" -lt 120 ] || { echo "$pending check(s) of pull request $NUMBER are still pending after an hour: nothing is merged" >&2; exit 1; }
        sleep "$POLL_SECS"
    done
}
settle
# A check that gave up waiting for the attestation is asked once more.
stale=$(forge pr checks "$NUMBER" --json bucket,completedAt,link --jq "[.[] | select((.bucket == \"fail\" or .bucket == \"cancel\") and .completedAt < \"$ATTESTED_AT\" and (.link | test(\"/runs/[0-9]+/\"))) | .link | capture(\"/runs/(?<id>[0-9]+)/\").id] | unique | .[]") || { echo "cannot read the checks of pull request $NUMBER" >&2; exit 2; }
if [ -n "$stale" ]; then
    for run in $stale; do
        forge run rerun "$run" --failed >&2 || { echo "cannot ask run $run again" >&2; exit 2; }
    done
    sleep "$POLL_SECS"
    settle
fi
# A skipped check is not a passed one, nor a refusal: only a bucket the forge
# calls fail or cancel stops the merge.
red=$(forge pr checks "$NUMBER" --json bucket,name --jq '[.[] | select(.bucket == "fail" or .bucket == "cancel") | .name] | join(", ")')
[ -z "$red" ] || { echo "the forge reports these checks not green on pull request $NUMBER: $red" >&2; exit 1; }
forge pr merge "$NUMBER" --merge --match-head-commit "$COMMIT" >&2
printf '{"merged":"%s","asked":true}' "$COMMIT"

set -eu
git -C "$REPO" fetch -q --no-tags "$REMOTE_NAME"
remote=$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse "refs/remotes/$REMOTE_NAME/$BASE")
git -C "$REPO" merge-base --is-ancestor "$COMMIT" "$remote" || { echo "the remote $BASE at $remote does not carry the reviewed $COMMIT" >&2; exit 1; }
if [ "$ALREADY" != true ]; then
    # **THE CANDIDATE'S ID IS NEVER ON THE TRUNK**: the forge writes its own
    # merge commit. What has to match is the tree, or what landed is not what
    # the gates were run on.
    landed=$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse "$remote^{tree}")
    validated=$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse "$CANDIDATE^{tree}")
    [ "$landed" = "$validated" ] || { echo "the trunk at $remote carries tree $landed, not the $validated the gates were run on" >&2; exit 1; }
fi
printf '{"remote_trunk":"%s"}' "$remote"

set -eu
cd "$REPO"
# An inherited GH_REPO would point a call at another repository: it goes before the first gh call.
unset GH_REPO
forge_as=$(git -C "$REPO" config --get sailor.forgeAs) || { echo "sailor.forgeAs is not declared on this tree: refusing to act as the machine's active account" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -n "$forge_as" ] || { echo "sailor.forgeAs is empty on this tree: refusing to act as the machine's active account" >&2; exit 1; }
env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_REPO gh auth token --user "$forge_as" >/dev/null || { echo "no forge token for the declared account $forge_as" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -z "${FORGE_REPO:-}" ] || export GH_REPO="$FORGE_REPO"
# An empty --user or an empty GH_TOKEN makes gh answer as the machine's active account.
forge() {
    who=$(git -C "$REPO" config --get sailor.forgeAs) && [ -n "$who" ] || { echo "sailor.forgeAs vanished from this tree: refusing" >&2; exit 1; }
    token=$(env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_REPO gh auth token --user "$who") && [ -n "$token" ] || { echo "no forge token for $who: refusing" >&2; exit 1; }
    if [ -n "${FORGE_REPO:-}" ]; then
        env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN -u GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN GH_REPO="$FORGE_REPO" GH_TOKEN="$token" gh "$@"
    else
        env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN -u GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN -u GH_REPO GH_TOKEN="$token" gh "$@"
    fi
}
tries=0
while :; do
    state=$(forge pr view "$NUMBER" --json state --jq .state)
    [ "$state" = MERGED ] && break
    tries=$((tries + 1))
    [ "$tries" -lt 20 ] || { echo "the host still reports pull request $NUMBER as $state after the trunk carries it" >&2; exit 1; }
    sleep 3
done
printf '{"number":%s,"state":"%s"}' "$NUMBER" "$state"

set -eu
[ -n "$TREE" ] || exit 0
git -C "$REPO" worktree unlock "$TREE" 2>/dev/null || true
git -C "$REPO" worktree remove --force "$TREE"
